mainTopic: Who recites the ברכה of שהחיינו at a פדיון הבן: the כהן or the father (אבי הבן)?
overview: The last piece of מסכת פסחים is a story about רבי שמלאי at a פדיון הבן. The people there ask him about the ברכות. They say it is obvious that the father recites the ברכה on the מצוה itself, 'על פדיון הבן'. Their real question is who recites שהחיינו. Is it the כהן, who gains the five סלעים, or the father, who does the מצוה? רבי שמלאי does not know, so he asks in the בית המדרש. They answer that the father recites both ברכות, and the גמרא rules this as הלכה. The amud ends with the הדרן, which closes פרק ערבי פסחים and the whole מסכת פסחים.

steps.title: רבי שמלאי at a פדיון הבן, and the obvious first blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמלאי attends a פדיון הבן and is asked a question. The questioners begin with what is obvious: the father recites the ברכה of 'על פדיון הבן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמלאי came to a פדיון הבן, and they asked him a question. They said: it is obvious that the father of the son recites the blessing 'Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us concerning the redemption of the son.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story and sets up a question. Before asking, the people state the part they are already sure about, so the real question can come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father is the one obligated in the מצוה of פדיון הבן, so he clearly recites the מצוה-ברכה. Saying 'פשיטא' marks this as settled ground. It narrows the doubt to the second ברכה only.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption of a firstborn son from a כהן with five סלעים
Happened to come / was present at

phrases.english: Rabbi Simlai happened to attend a redemption of a son,
they asked him:
It is obvious that over the redemption of the son,
"Who sanctified us with His commandments
and commanded us concerning the redemption of the son"
the father of the son recites it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי אִיקְּלַע לְפִדְיוֹן הַבֵּן, בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new short story-based discussion about the order and assignment of ברכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The father recites the מצוה-ברכה 'על פדיון הבן'; this is treated as obvious.

steps.title: Who says שהחיינו: the כהן or the father?
steps.stepSummary: The real question: does the כהן or the father recite שהחיינו at a פדיון הבן?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the blessing 'Blessed ... Who has kept us alive, sustained us, and brought us to this time': does the כהן recite it, or does the father of the son recite it?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the people ask their real question. They want to know who should say שהחיינו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שהחיינו is a ברכה of joy over a new occasion. Two people have a stake in this event, the כהן and the father. So it is unclear whose joy the ברכה belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who has kept us alive', the blessing over a new or joyous occasion
The priest who receives the redemption money

phrases.english: "Blessed ... Who has kept us alive, sustained us,
and brought us to this time":
does the kohen recite it,
or does the father of the son recite it?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֵן מְבָרֵךְ, אוֹ אֲבִי הַבֵּן מְבָרֵךְ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the obvious ברכה to the doubtful one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which person, the כהן or אבי הבן, is the proper one to recite שהחיינו at a פדיון הבן.

steps.title: The reasoning behind each side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains both sides: the כהן gains money, while the father performs the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the כהן recite it, because benefit comes into his hands? Or does the father recite it, because he is doing the מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each answer makes sense. This sharpens the question before the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view: שהחיינו is for the one who gains something, and the כהן receives five סלעים. The other view: שהחיינו belongs to the one doing the מצוה, and that is the father. The question is whether the ברכה follows benefit or the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Since he is performing the מצוה

phrases.english: Does the kohen recite it,
since benefit comes into his hands,
or does the father of the son recite it,
since he is the one performing the מצוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of the question from step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether שהחיינו follows the one who benefits or the one who performs the מצוה.

steps.title: The study hall answers: the father says both
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמלאי did not know the answer, so he asked in the בית המדרש. They told him the father recites both ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not have the answer, so he went and asked in the study hall. They told him: the father of the son recites two blessings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמלאי admits he does not know and goes to ask others. The בית המדרש answers that the father says both ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Two' means 'על פדיון הבן' and שהחיינו. So שהחיינו follows the one doing the מצוה, not the one gaining money. The כהן recites neither ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not have it in hand; he did not know the answer

phrases.english: He did not have the answer in hand,
so he went and asked it in the study hall.
They said to him:
The father of the son recites two blessings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: אֲבִי הַבֵּן מְבָרֵךְ שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in steps 2 and 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The father recites both 'על פדיון הבן' and שהחיינו; the ברכה follows the one doing the מצוה.

steps.title: The final ruling: the father recites two blessings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules as הלכה that the father recites both ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: the father of the son recites two blessings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the answer of the בית המדרש the official הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating the answer with 'והלכתא' turns a reported answer into a binding ruling. In practice, at a פדיון הבן the father says both ברכות.
steps.whatToRemember: At a פדיון הבן, אבי הבן recites both ברכות: 'על פדיון הבן' and שהחיינו. שהחיינו goes with the one doing the מצוה, not the one who gains the money.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is practiced to this day: at every פדיון הבן the father says both ברכות.

phrases.english: And the halakha is:
The father of the son recites two blessings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes the answer of step 4 the binding הלכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הלכה: אבי הבן recites both ברכות at a פדיון הבן.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing ערבי פסחים and מסכת פסחים
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for פרק ערבי פסחים, which also marks the end of מסכת פסחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, ערבי פסחים, and מסכת פסחים is completed.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the הדרן, the traditional closing line of a פרק. Here it also closes the entire מסכת פסחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the legal discussion. It says we will come back to this פרק. Since this is the last פרק, it also announces that the מסכת is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the closing formula of a פרק
The name of the tenth and final פרק of פסחים

phrases.english: We will return to you, Arvei Pesachim,
and Tractate Pesachim is concluded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formal closing after the final הלכה of the פרק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק ערבי פסחים and מסכת פסחים are complete.
